Alright, I've just finished the core game simulation in `game.js` – it defines weapons, player logic, bots, economy, round flow, everything that drives the match. The next major component is the HUD, which is going to be the visual overlay that the player sees: crosshair, viewmodel, muzzle flash, tracers, damage numbers, hitmarkers, radar, kill feed, health/armor displays, and the buy menu UI. 

First, I need to think about what this HUD module needs to import. It will definitely need the weapon definitions (including melee flag, scoped flag, reload times, etc.) and the armor price constant from `game.js`. It will also need the map geometry (BOXES and material IDs) to draw the radar footprint, so those come from `map.js`. The crosshair rendering is driven by the settings schema, so I should bring in `crosshairCSS` and `renderCrosshair` from `settings.js`. 

Next, the class structure. I’ll create an `HUD` class that takes the `game` instance and the `settings` object in its constructor. Inside, I’ll grab the overlay canvas (`#overlay`) and its 2D context, as well as the crosshair element (`#crosshair`). I’ll also set up arrays for transient visual effects: `tracers`, `dmgNumbers`, and a killfeed array. Timers for flash, hitmarker, vignette, and weapon switch animation will be stored as floats. I’ll keep track of the last weapon to trigger a switch animation.

I need a `resize` method that ensures the canvas dimensions match its CSS size – this is crucial for high-DPI scaling and for the radar to render correctly. The `worldToScreen` method will convert 3D world positions to 2D screen coordinates using the camera’s position, forward/right/up vectors, and field of view. I’ll calculate depth (`dz`) to cull points behind the camera, then compute normalized device coordinates and map them to pixel space.

For handling shot events, `onShot(info, cam)` will be called with hit info. It should trigger a muzzle flash timer, iterate over each hit, convert the hit point to screen space, and push a tracer line from the gun muzzle (roughly 62% width, 78% height) to the hit location. If the hit was on a bot and damage numbers are enabled, I’ll also push a damage number at the hit point (offset a bit upward). If the shot registered a hit, I’ll set the hitmarker timer and note if it was a headshot.

`onPlayerDamage()` will just set the vignette timer to give a red overlay when the player takes damage.

`addKillfeed(text, head)` will push a new entry onto the killfeed array, respecting the user setting for showing the feed, and cap the list at five entries.

The crosshair needs to reflect weapon spread and movement. `updateCrosshair()` will compute spread in pixels based on the current weapon’s spread value plus a velocity factor, then call `renderCrosshair` with the CSS generated by `crosshairCSS`. If the player is scoped, the crosshair element should be hidden.

The main `draw(dt, cam)` method will be called each frame. It will:
1. Call `resize()`.
2. Clear the canvas.
3. Early‑out if there’s no player.
4. Update and render tracers (fade over 0.08 s).
5. Update and render damage numbers (fade over 0.9 s, larger font for headshots).
6. Render the hitmarker if its timer is active.
7. If viewmodel is enabled and the player isn’t scoped, call `drawViewmodel`.
8. If the player is scoped, draw the black overlay with a circular scope cutout and crosshair lines.
9. If radar is enabled, call `drawRadar`.
10. Render the damage vignette if its timer is still positive.
11. Render a low‑HP pulse when health ≤ 30.

`drawViewmodel` will handle the weapon silhouette. I need to fetch the current weapon definition (`def`) and handle melee vs ranged. The weapon switch animation (`weaponSwitchT`) should start at 0.25 s when the weapon changes. Bobbing is optional via the `controls.viewBobbing` setting, and recoil is taken from `game.recoil`. The silhouette will be drawn with simple rectangles for barrel, body, grip, mag, and optional scope, plus a neon accent stripe. If the weapon is melee, draw a blade shape. Finally, if the flash timer is active, draw a radial gradient muzzle flash at the muzzle location.

`drawRadar` will render a small minimap in the top‑left corner. I’ll use a fixed size (130 px) with padding, draw a semi‑transparent background, then iterate over `BOXES` to draw wall footprints (skip floor and very thin boxes). Bots are drawn as red circles, the player as a cyan circle with a direction line.

The DOM stats panel needs an `updateDOM` method that writes to various HUD elements (`hud-hp`, `hud-armor`, etc.). I’ll create a helper `setText(id, txt)` that only updates the DOM if the text actually changed (to avoid unnecessary reflows). This method will also handle the killfeed DOM: decrement each entry’s timer, filter out expired entries, and rebuild the innerHTML of `#killfeed`. The timer display should show “BUY X” during the buy phase or a MM:SS clock otherwise, with a warning class when the live phase timer is low.

Lastly, the buy menu UI is a separate function `buildBuyMenu(container, game, onBuy)`. It will populate a grid of weapon cards and an armor card, using the `WEAPONS` definitions for name, damage, RPM, and price. Clicking a card calls the supplied `onBuy` callback.

All of this needs to be written to a new file at the correct path: `/home/lane/AIArchives/archives/neonstrike/app/public/js/hud.js`. I’ll include the imports at the top, then the `HUD` class with all its methods,
